learning: No prior evidence. After the first race, check whether line loss or oscillation dominates, then adjust kp/kd before changing geometry.
notes: Baseline package: the Builder's symmetric 5-sensor geometry with a proportional-dominant controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0) and base speed 1.4. Expected to be untuned because no race data exists yet.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback yet. The geometry is the Builder's baseline and is used unchanged: five sensors at 12 mm spacing (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, y = 0.05 m), 12 mm footprints, wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.16 x 0.12 m. All values are inside the contract limits. The sensor span of 48 mm is about twice the 25 mm tape, so the line stays visible through moderate offsets. Sensors sit ahead of the axle, so the controller sees the line before the wheels reach it. The controller uses weights proportional to sensor x: [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. Because positive x is left and positive signal steers left, this pushes the robot back toward the line in the correct direction. kp = 2.0 gives a turn of about 700 PWM counts between wheels for a moderate signal, which is a cautious starting gain. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on a short 3 s course. kd = 0.2 damps the response without much noise amplification. base_speed = 1.4 (PWM 70%) is a compromise: it is fast enough to approach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, but not so fast that the first untuned controller loses the line. line_loss = 'last_direction' lets the robot recover toward the side it was last on, which suits the curved tracks. I expect completion on the development tracks, but this is untested.
